summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for presumed acute pyelonephritis following right flank pain and a positive urine culture showing E. coli. He had recently completed a course of antibiotics for a prior pyelonephritis but continued to feel unwell. During his hospitalization, he remained afebrile, and his leukocytosis improved. Renal ultrasound showed no abscess or hydronephrosis, with stable findings compared to prior imaging. His chronic kidney disease and mild metabolic acidosis were noted but stable. He was transitioned to oral cefpodoxime and discharged home with instructions to complete a 14-day antibiotic course and follow up with primary care, infectious disease, urology, and orthopedics for ongoing management. His paraplegia and recent motor vehicle accident with suspected rotator cuff injury were also addressed in discharge planning.
problems: Acute pyelonephritis without lesion of renal medullary necrosis
